content: If you are allergic to peginterferon alfa-2a, polyethylene glycol (PEG), or any other substances, inform your doctor or pharmacist before using this medication. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. This medication can increase your susceptibility to infections or exacerbate existing infections. Avoid contact with individuals who have contagious infections, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. Notify your healthcare provider that you are using peginterferon alfa-2a before receiving any vaccinations or immunizations. Peginterferon alfa-2a may cause dizziness. Consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can intensify this effect. Refrain from driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you are confident you can do so safely. Avoid alcoholic beverages. Children may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medication, particularly mental or mood changes such as severe depression or suicidal thoughts/attempts. Peginterferon alfa-2a may also slow a child’s growth, potentially resulting in a lower-than-expected final adult height. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your doctor. You should not become pregnant while using peginterferon alfa-2a, as it may harm an unborn baby. Discuss reliable forms of birth control with your healthcare provider while using this medication. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., blood counts, thyroid tests, virus levels, kidney/liver function, triglyceride levels, eye exams) should be conducted before starting this medication and periodically during its use. Do not switch brands of interferon without consulting your doctor or pharmacist. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember, provided it is within two days of the scheduled dose. Administer your next dose on the usual day. Store this medication in the refrigerator, away from light and moisture. Do not freeze it. Do not leave it out of the refrigerator for more than 24 hours. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This medication may rarely cause or worsen serious medical conditions, including mental/mood problems (e.g., depression), autoimmune conditions (e.g., lupus, rheumatoid arthritis), blood vessel problems (e.g., heart disease), or infections. Close monitoring by your doctor may reduce your risk. Report any serious symptoms or side effects to your doctor immediately. Peginterferon alfa-2a is used alone or in combination with other medications to treat chronic hepatitis B and chronic hepatitis C, which are viral infections of the liver. It works by reducing the amount of hepatitis virus in the body and enhancing your immune system’s ability to combat the infection. It is not known whether peginterferon can cure hepatitis B or C or prevent the transmission of the virus to others. Before using peginterferon alfa-2a, read the Medication Guide and Instructions for Use provided by your pharmacist. Consult your healthcare professional on how to prepare and use this medication. Inject it under the skin as directed by your doctor, usually once a week. The injection is typically administered in the abdomen or thigh. Avoid injecting near the belly button or waistline. Dosage is based on your medical condition, lab tests, and response to treatment. For a more comfortable injection, allow the medication to warm to room temperature as directed in the Instructions for Use. Do not warm it in any other way (e.g., microwave or hot water). Do not shake the medication. Inspect the product for particles or discoloration before use. If either is present, do not use the liquid. Clean the injection site with rubbing alcohol before each dose. Rotate injection sites to minimize skin injury. To reduce bruising, avoid rubbing the injection site after administration. Use this medication regularly to achieve the most benefit. Many individuals experience flu-like symptoms such as headache, fatigue, fever, chills, and muscle aches, which usually subside after the first few weeks of treatment. You can minimize these side effects by injecting the medication at bedtime and using fever reducers/pain relievers like acetaminophen before each dose. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Other side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dry mouth, loss of appetite, dizziness, trouble sleeping, or redness/swelling at the injection site. Tooth and gum problems may also occur during treatment. Dry mouth can exacerbate these issues. Prevent dry mouth by drinking plenty of water or using a saliva substitute. Brush your teeth thoroughly at least twice daily and schedule regular dental exams. Temporary hair loss may occur. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. However, it may cause serious mental/mood changes that could worsen during treatment or after your last dose. It may also weaken your immune system, increasing your susceptibility to serious (rarely fatal) infections or worsening existing infections. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
